content.title: Patients with cancer

recommendations.text: An invasive strategy is recommended in cancer patients presenting with high-risk ACS with expected survival ≥6 months.
recommendations.notes: Applies to cancer patients with expected survival >= 6 months.

recommendations.text: A temporary interruption of cancer therapy is recommended in patients in whom the cancer therapy is suspected to be a contributing cause of ACS.
recommendations.notes: Interrupt cancer therapy when it is suspected to contribute to acute coronary syndrome.

recommendations.text: A conservative non-invasive strategy should be considered in ACS patients with poor cancer prognosis (i.e. with expected survival <6 months) and/or very high bleeding risk.
recommendations.notes: For patients with expected survival <6 months or very high bleeding risk.

recommendations.text: Aspirin is not recommended in cancer patients with a platelet count <10,000/µL.
recommendations.notes: Absolute platelet threshold for avoiding aspirin therapy.

recommendations.text: Clopidogrel is not recommended in cancer patients with a platelet count <30,000/µL.
recommendations.notes: Absolute platelet threshold for avoiding clopidogrel.

recommendations.text: In ACS patients with cancer and <50,000/µL platelet count, prasugrel or ticagrelor are not recommended.
recommendations.notes: Avoid prasugrel or ticagrelor when platelets are below 50,000/µL.

footnotes: c Anticancer therapies associated with high risk of ACS (very common [>10%]) include the listed agents.
d Related to advanced cancer stage and/or severe irreversible non-cardiovascular comorbidities.
